children: Harvey Norman's bull at Bell Potter sees growing macro headwinds for the Australian appliance and furniture retailer. Analyst Chami Ratnapala keeps a buy rating on the stock but tells clients in a note that a challenging operating environment showed up in Harvey Norman's fiscal 2026 results, with some sizable second-half misses in its key franchising division. She warns that the start of fiscal 2027 featured declining comparable sales in most major markets, and that consumer sentiment is weakening in Australia as shoppers brace for further interest-rate rises. Bell Potter cuts its target price by 17% to 5.00 Australian dollars. Shares are down 2.5% at A$4.175. (stuart.condie@wsj.com)
